h: Pairing play with a proper Leicester day
p: Little ones tend to go hardest in the first hour, so plan for that. A morning visit lets them charge round while they're fresh, then the afternoon can be something slower, like a stroll, a picnic or a trip to one of the city's family-friendly museums.

Let the kids lead. Some children make a beeline for the role-play shops and stay there happily, others want to try everything in quick succession. Both are absolutely fine. If you've got siblings of different ages, try giving each of them a turn to pick the next activity, so nobody feels dragged along.

Socks are a must for play centres, so pop a pair in for everyone. Spare clothes and a towel come in handy too, particularly with water and messy play on the menu, and a drink bottle each saves endless trips to the counter.

If you've got time to spare, Leicester has plenty more to fill the day. Bradgate Park, just outside the city, is a huge stretch of open countryside where deer roam freely and there are ruins of the old house to explore. It's brilliant for a walk and a picnic on a dry day.

Leicester Cathedral, where King Richard III was reburied, is a short walk from the visitor centre that tells his story, and the city's indoor and outdoor market is great for a browse and a bite. For train fans, the Great Central Railway at Loughborough, a short drive north, runs heritage steam trains and makes a cracking extra day out.
Weekday mornings in term time tend to be quieter, which suits younger toddlers who find busy play spaces a bit overwhelming.
